extracted.intended_audience: machine learning researchers and formal-verification practitioners (authors/users of proof assistants such as Isabelle/HOL and Coq)
extracted.subtask_description: Developing and evaluating large-language-model methods that generate whole proofs (not step-by-step) for theorems in proof assistants, and repairing generated proofs using a fine-tuned repair model. The work is empirical and targets automation of formal verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whole-proof generation feasibility and effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Whole-proof generation using transformers is possible and is as effective as search-based techniques without requiring costly search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion favors models that can produce entire proofs in one generation pass (rather than predicting one proof step at a time). The bar is parity with search-based, stepwise techniques in effectiveness while avoiding the computational cost of search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof repair using additional context
rubrics_metrics.description: Giving the learned model additional context, such as a prior failed proof attempt and the ensuing error message, results in proof repair and further improves automated proof generation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Models should accept and exploit contextual signals (failed attempts, error messages) to produce repaired/corrected proofs. Evaluation should show repair improves success over generation-only approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine generation and repair to increase proving power
rubrics_metrics.description: We combine this proof generation model with a fine-tuned repair model to repair generated proofs, further increasing proving power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The pipeline approach (generate whole proof → detect/receive failure context → apply repair model) is an explicit design criterion. Measure increased proving power from the combined pipeline versus generation alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model training and fine-tuning regimen
rubrics_metrics.description: Use large language models, trained on natural language text and code and fine-tuned on proofs, to generate whole proofs for theorems at once, rather than one step at a time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion covers the data and fine-tuning strategy: pretraining on natural language and code plus supervised fine-tuning on proof corpora. Methods should report these training sources and justify their role in whole-proof performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical evaluation on a substantial benchmark
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate it on a benchmark of 6,336 Isabelle/HOL theorems and their proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect large-scale, reproducible evaluation on a named benchmark (6,336 Isabelle/HOL theorems here). Performance should be reported over this corpus to substantiate claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-of-the-art automated proof synthesis
rubrics_metrics.description: We establish a new state of the art for fully automated proof synthesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims of SOTA must be supported by comparative empirical metrics (success rates, benchmarks). Papers should compare to prior top tools and report clear improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvement over prior tool (Thor) measured by additional theorem coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Baldur improves on the state-of-the-art tool, Thor, by automatically generating proofs for an additional 8.7% of the theorems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance comparisons should include absolute percentage-point improvements (here, +8.7% over Thor). Use clear baselines and report the delta in proved-theorem counts/percentages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combined-system success reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Together, Baldur and Thor can prove 65.7% of the theorems fully automatically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report combined or ensemble/system-level success metrics where relevant (e.g., combining multiple tools yields higher overall coverage). Provide the combined success percentage and clarify how systems interact/are composed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prototype implementation and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: We reify our method in a prototype, Baldur, and evaluate it on a benchmark of 6,336 Isabelle/HOL theorems and their proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion emphasizes producing a working prototype and publishing evaluation artifacts (implementation, benchmark details, possibly code/data) to permit reproduction of reported results.
